title: AI service advisor for fixed operations
summary: A practical resource center for dealership AI service advisors, call overflow, service scheduling, reminders, and fixed-operations growth.
body_markdown:
## Start with service capacity and booking rules


An AI service advisor should not be treated as a generic answering service. It needs approved information, department-specific routing, appointment eligibility rules, escalation paths, and a reliable source of availability before it can complete useful work.


The first deployment should solve one observable problem, such as after-hours booking or queue overflow. That makes it possible to compare completion, handoff, and appointment outcomes against a real baseline.


## Keep judgment with the service team


Routine booking, confirmation, reminders, and basic routing can be automated within clear policy. Diagnosis, safety concerns, pricing exceptions, complex repair-order questions, and upset customers need a defined human path.


The goal is not to remove the advisor. It is to keep advisors focused on work that requires context and judgment while customers still receive a timely response.
